classification.difficultyReason: First establish parallel lines using an angle-property converse, then use parallel-line angle properties to find an unknown.

content.prompt: In each diagram below, give a reason why $AB\parallel CD$. Hence, find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$.

spec.description: Triangle OCD with A on OC and B on OD, joined by AB. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Angle OAB and angle OCD are both 42 degrees; angle CDO is 54 degrees; angle OBA is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because corresponding angles are equal ($42^\circ$). $\beta=54^\circ$ (corresponding angles).
answer.worked:
$\angle OAB=\angle OCD=42^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because corresponding angles are equal.

$\beta=54^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Two horizontal lines with upper points A,U,V,B and lower points C,X,W,D; transversals UX and VW.
spec.mathematics: Angles AUX and UXW are 68 degrees; angle UVW is 100 degrees; angle VWD is alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal ($68^\circ$). $\alpha=100^\circ$ (alternate angles).
answer.worked:
$\angle AUX=\angle UXW=68^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal.

$\alpha=100^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Horizontal AB above CD, with diagonals AD and BC intersecting at V.
spec.mathematics: Angles BAV and CDV are both 43 degrees; angle ABV is 28 degrees; angle VCD is gamma.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal ($43^\circ$). $\gamma=28^\circ$ (alternate angles).
answer.worked:
$\angle BAV=\angle CDV=43^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal.

$\gamma=28^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABDC with vertical AC, horizontal AB and CD, and sloping BD; right-angle marks at A and C.
spec.mathematics: Angles CAB and ACD are right angles; angle CDB is 71 degrees; angle ABD is theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because co-interior angles are supplementary ($90^\circ+90^\circ=180^\circ$). $\theta=109^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle CAB+\angle ACD=90^\circ+90^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because co-interior angles are supplementary.

Co-interior angles on transversal $BD$ are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}\theta+71^\circ&=180^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ-71^\circ\\\theta&=109^\circ\end{align*}$$
